mcas.excerpt: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are pruritic inflammatory skin diseases that share partly overlapping mast-cell-related pathways, including IgE/FcεRI signaling, type 2 inflammation, neuroimmune signaling, and lipid mediator pathways. Yet they usually produce distinct phenotypes: transient wheals and angioedema in CSU and persistent eczematous lesions with inflammation in AD.

mcas.title: IL-33/ST2 signalling in pediatric food allergy and eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review of human and preclinical evidence.
mcas.authors: Grama, Monica, Săsăran, Maria Oana, Stan Muntean, Ana, Coman, Delia et al.
mcas.excerpt: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is an epithelial-derived member of the IL-1 cytokine family that functions as an alarmin and signals through the ST2 receptor, upstream of type 2 inflammation. Together with thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) and IL-25, it constitutes an epithelial alarmin triad that orchestrates barrier-related immune responses.

mcas.title: Colonic Mast Cell Density and Diarrhoea: Evidence Against a Threshold Effect in Biopsies From 3508 Patients.
mcas.authors: Langreiter, Marlena, Genta, Robert M, Schreiner, Philipp
mcas.excerpt: Elevated mast cell (MC) counts in colonic biopsies are frequently observed in patients with chronic diarrhoea or unspecific abdominal symptoms, potentially leading to a diagnosis of mast cell activation syndrome. However, the clinical relevance of MC quantification in this setting remains controversial.
